Assembly Stdio Features

Editor, interpreter and debugger for IJVM and Intel 8088 assembly

Getting Started
Open a .jas/.ijvm or .asm/.a8088 file, then select Run or Debug in the execution toolbar. The program output, the input and the messages appear in the terminal. The memory viewer shows the state of the program.

Window and Title Bar

  • Custom window frame - Same layout on macOS, Linux and Windows, resizable from every edge
  • Working directory - The title shows the current directory
    • Double-click to maximize or restore the window
    • Ctrl+Click (Cmd+Click on macOS) to open the directory in the file browser
    • Drag to move the window
  • Resizable panels - Drag the border between the editor and the debugger

Files and Help Menus

  • Change Working Path - Select or create the folder of your source files
  • Open - Open a source file; an open file activates its tab
  • New - Create a file; the dialog asks before it replaces a file
  • Save as... - Save the current file with a new name and the same extension
  • Help - This page, the 8088 instructions and the IJVM instructions

Code Editor

  • Syntax highlighting - The lexer follows the file extension
  • Tabs - One tab per file; hidden tabs are in the overflow menu
  • Automatic saving - Edits are saved to disk while you type and before each run
  • Search - Ctrl+F, with plain text or regular expressions
  • Zoom - Ctrl +, Ctrl -, Ctrl 0, Ctrl + wheel, or pinch
  • Line commands - Ctrl+Shift+Up/Down moves the selected lines
  • Execution line - In debug mode a green arrow and a green background mark the next instruction; the editor scrolls to it while its file is in the selected tab

Execution Toolbar

  • Run - Execute the current file without pauses
  • Debug - Pause before the first instruction
  • Stop - End the program at any time
  • Step - In debug mode, execute 1 or 10 instructions
  • Automatic stepping - Execute one instruction every 500 ms, 1 s, 2 s, 3 s, 4 s, 5 s or 10 s
  • HEX / DEC - Show the memory values in hexadecimal (default) or in decimal; the switch updates every value at once

Memory Viewer

  • Header - The program counter, the next instruction with its source line, the scope and the language
  • IJVM - CONSTANTS and STACK
    • Each method frame shows its variables first, then its operand stack by word address
    • A called method appears inside the frame of its caller
  • 8088 - REGISTERS, STACK, MEMORY and FLAGS
    • The stack shows each word by address; the words of a subroutine, from its return address down, are inside a group with its label
  • Change animation - A new value flashes green; a removed value flashes red
  • Follow - In debug mode the viewer scrolls to each new value or frame
  • Input light - A light blue light runs around the header while the program waits for input
  • Copy - The copy button of a value puts name: value on the clipboard

Terminal

  • Program output - The output appears while the program runs
  • Messages - Only the tag has a color: [INFO] light blue, [WARNING] yellow, [EXCEPTION] red; the text is light gray
  • Prompt - After each run, a separator bar and the file >> prompt appear again
  • Search - Ctrl+F in the terminal
  • Clear - Ctrl+L or Ctrl+Shift+K, also in the context menu
  • Zoom - Same keys and gestures as the editor

Program Input

How to type an input
When the program executes IN (IJVM) or the _GETCHAR system call (8088), it waits and the light runs around the memory viewer header. Type the characters in the terminal and press Enter.
RuleDetails
One character, one inputEach input instruction reads one character. The line 12; gives three inputs: '1', '2' and ';'. Typing them on one line or on three lines gives the same result.
ValueThe program receives the character code, not the digit: '1' is 49 (0x31). Subtract 0x30 to get a digit.
Maximum value255 (0xFF). Each input is one byte, so every character must have a code from 0 to 255. The terminal does not send a line with another character and shows a warning.
EnterEnter sends the line. It does not send a newline character, and an empty line sends nothing.
End of a numberThe course programs end a number with ; (0x3B). Type ; after the digits.
Typing aheadThe characters wait in a queue until the program reads them, up to 4096 characters.

Addresses

ItemIJVM8088
Program counterByte address in the method area. main starts at 0; each other method follows in source order after a 4-byte header (parameter count and local count).Byte address in the text segment, from 0. The size of each instruction follows the 8086 encoding; a jump uses the short form when its target is in range.
Instruction size1 byte, 2 bytes for BIPUSH, ILOAD, ISTORE, and 3 bytes for GOTO, IFEQ, IFLT, IF_ICMPEQ, IINC, LDC_W, INVOKEVIRTUAL. Labels take no space.Opcode, ModR/M byte, displacement and immediate, as in the 8086.
StackWord addresses. The frame of main starts at 0x8000 with its variables. A called method takes the address of its OBJREF as its base (LV): the link pointer, the parameters, the variables, the saved PC and the saved LV come before its operand stack.Offsets in the stack segment. CALL pushes the byte address of the next instruction and RET jumps back to it.
